transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, it’s not anything too dramatic, I don’t think… but I’ve noticed I’m having trouble keeping up when people are talking to me. Like at the museum, someone will be telling me about the next art walk, and I’m looking right at them, trying to listen, but then I realize I missed the middle part of what they said. So I have to ask them to repeat it. I feel a little embarrassed about it, honestly.
Do you find it hard to follow conversations or instructions, especially when there are multiple steps or when things are said quickly?

Yes… I think so, at least a little. It’s mostly when someone’s talking right to me, like at the museum about the next art walk, and I’m trying to listen, I really am. But then I notice I’ve missed the middle part of what they said, and I have to ask them to run it by me again. It’s not constant, I don’t think, but it happens enough that it’s embarrassing.
Do you find it hard to focus or sustain your attention in other situations, like reading a book or following a conversation in a quiet room without distractions?

Yes, I think so… not terribly, but it does happen. Like if I sit down with a gallery packet or some notes, I’ll start off fine and feel like I’m reading it. Then after a few minutes, my eyes are still going over the page, but my mind has sort of gone somewhere else. I’ll realize I didn’t really take in what I just read and have to go back over the same part again. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks like organizing your schedule or completing projects at work or home?

A little, yes. I don’t want to overstate it, but if I sit down with a gallery packet or some notes, I’ll start off okay. Then after a few minutes I realize my eyes are still moving along the page, but my mind has drifted off somewhere else. So I end up reading the same part again. I’m not sure if that counts as the kind of focus problem you mean.

Do you find that these difficulties with attention or focus have been happening for a long time, like even when you were a child, or do you feel like this is something that started more recently in your life?

I think it goes back pretty far, yes. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but even in grade school my report cards would say things like “daydreams” or “needs reminders to finish work.” And my mother used to sit beside me when I did homework, just to keep me on track, even before I was twelve. So… I guess it isn’t exactly new.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated, especially in situations where you’re expected to remain still?

Not really, I don’t think. I mean, I might shift around a bit like anyone does if I’m sitting too long, but I wouldn’t say I feel driven to get up or that I can’t stay seated. At least, not that I’ve noticed. Is that what you mean?
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I have off days like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling really down or losing interest in things. At least not in a way that stands out to me. Does that answer it okay?
Have you had days where you felt down or hopeless, or where things just didn’t give you the same pleasure they used to?

No, not really. I mean, I have normal days where I’m a little blah or tired of things, but I wouldn’t call it hopeless or like I can’t enjoy anything. I still get some pleasure from the usual things, as far as I can tell. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
